To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) PPA is a robust phenomenon that occurs in mice with high-frequency (8-16 kHz) hearing loss, but is not seen in normal-hearing mice, 2) PPI is observed in all subject groups, 3) PPI is prolonged in 5-month old C57 mice, 4) PPI is frequency specific, and 5) prolonged PPI is observed only in mice that show over-representation of high-frequency neurons in the auditory cortex.

prepulse augmentation (amplification of the startle response by a prepulse) occurs in 5-month old C57 mice, but not in 1-month-old or 5-month-old mice of the same strain with high-frequency hearing impairment.
5-month-old mice with a high-frequency hearing loss exhibit prolonged PPI and PPA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modification of the acoustic starttle response (ASR) by a brief acoustic stimulus, termed a prepulse (S2).
the modification of the acoustic starttle response (ASR) in mice with normal or abnormal hearing, and the effects of these modifications on prepulse inhibition (PPL) of the ASR.
how the central auditory system responds to the loss of input from the peripheral auditory system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 5-month-old, hearing-impaired CBA/Ca mice and the 5-month, hearing-impaired, high-frequency, C57BL/ 6J mice exhibited prepulse inhibition (P1) with interstimulus intervals of 10- 100ms, and prepulse augmentation (P2) with an interstimulus interval of 2ms.
the acoustic startle reflex in mice is a useful tool for investigating auditory plasticity.

the acoustic startle reflex of C57 mice with hearing loss is modified in two ways: (1) PPA of startle occurs with short ISIs (2 ms); and (2) PPI occurs with long ISIs (200-500 ms) and is prolonged compared with normal-hearing mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PPA and prolonged PPI occur in hearing-impaired mice and are associated with a frequency-dependent over-representation of high frequencies in the central nervous system.
hearing loss in C57 mice leads to overrepresentation of high-frequency tones in the auditory cortex and that this overrepresentation is reflected by prolonged PPI.
PPI and PPA are not necessarily linked, and that the PPI/PPI augmentation phenomenon may be a useful tool in studying central plasticity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PPI is a robust phenomenon that can be used as a tool for studying neural plasticity in the auditory system.
hearing-impaired CBA/Ca mice and C57 mice with normal hearing show PPA and PPI with short ISIs, whereas only the latter group exhibits prolonged PPI at long ISIs.

the acoustic startle system of mice with high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss exhibits a unique form of prepulse modification that may have implications for understanding the neural plasticity of hearing loss.
